detailed_rationale:
Data Patterns (India) is an integrated defence and aerospace electronics company (radars, electronic warfare, avionics, missile electronics) supplying DRDO, the armed forces and defence PSUs, with a near debt-free balance sheet (D/E ~0.003x, interest coverage 31x) and strong return ratios (ROE 14.7%, ROCE 20.8%). The quant data shows a 3-year revenue CAGR of 26.9% and 1-year growth of 30.5%, but the freshest print (Q1 FY27, quarter ended June 2026) shows the growth engine decelerating: revenue rose 16.8% YoY to Rs 116 crore while standalone net profit actually fell 13% YoY to Rs 22 crore (from Rs 25.5 crore), as operating costs outpaced revenue gains and operational EBITDA slipped ~2% YoY. The order book stood at Rs 928 crore as of June 2026, up from Rs 730 crore a year earlier (~27% YoY), which gives reasonable revenue visibility (roughly 2x annualized book-to-bill) but is itself lumpy in a defence-order business where large contract timing swings quarter results.

The stock trades at ~85x trailing earnings, a multiple that only makes sense if the company sustains high-20s/30%+ compounding for several more years with margin expansion, not the high-teens growth and margin compression just posted. Defence indigenization (Atmanirbhar Bharat), rising defence capex, and an emerging export opportunity for radar/EW systems are genuine structural tailwinds that support a premium multiple versus the broader capital goods space, but the latest quarter is a legitimate data point that growth is normalizing off a small base and margins are not a straight line up. This is a quality, clean-balance-sheet compounder priced for perfection; the call is about whether today's price already contains tomorrow's growth.
recommendation_rationale: Quant composite is Hold on both windows and nothing in the fresh research overturns that: this is a genuinely high-quality, debt-free defence electronics franchise, but at ~85x earnings with the latest quarter showing decelerating revenue growth (16.8% YoY) and a YoY profit decline, the valuation embeds continued hypergrowth that the business has not just demonstrated. That is a valuation-quality tension consistent with Hold, not a business-quality problem that would justify a Sell call (which is not available to me on a quant Hold in any case).
summary: Data Patterns is a well-run, debt-free defence electronics business benefiting from India's defence indigenization push, with a healthy and growing order book. The most recent quarter showed slower revenue growth and a dip in profit as costs rose faster than sales, and the stock's rich valuation leaves little room for further disappointment. We rate it a Hold: good business, but the price already assumes a lot of future growth.
positive_para: Debt-free balance sheet (D/E ~0.003x) with 31x interest coverage gives full flexibility to fund capacity and R&D without dilution risk. Order book of Rs 928 crore (up ~27% YoY) provides multi-quarter revenue visibility in a niche (radar, EW, avionics) with high entry barriers (DRDO/armed-forces qualification cycles) that keeps competition limited. Structural tailwind from rising defence capex and indigenization mandates, plus an emerging export angle for indigenous defence electronics, support a multi-year growth runway beyond the domestic order book alone.
negative_para: The latest quarter is the clearest read yet that hypergrowth is normalizing: revenue growth decelerated to 16.8% YoY (versus 26.9% 3-year and 30.5% trailing 1-year CAGRs in the quant data) and standalone net profit fell 13% YoY as costs rose faster than revenue — a genuine margin/earnings-quality wobble, not a one-off gain to explain away. At ~85x trailing earnings, the stock has very little valuation cushion if growth continues normalizing toward the high-teens/low-20s rather than the 30%+ pace embedded in the current multiple; defence order timing is also inherently lumpy quarter to quarter, so a soft print can as easily repeat as reverse.
reverse_dcf_judgment: At ~85x trailing EPS, the market is pricing in sustained 25-30%+ compounding with margin expansion for several more years. The Q1 FY27 print (revenue +16.8% YoY, PAT -13% YoY) is the first clear evidence the growth rate is normalizing off its small base while margins compressed rather than expanded — a mismatch against what the multiple needs. The order book (Rs 928 crore, ~2x annualized revenue) supports continued double-digit growth and some multiple justification given the quality/moat of the defence-electronics niche, but does not obviously support a re-acceleration back to 30%+. Call: rich, not obviously cheap even for a high-quality compounder.
